name: extract-word-content
description:
Words by what they hold; a word is tested as written, with its punctuation («красный,» does not end in «ный»).

kind: "starts", "ends", "contains" (with pattern); "only_latin" (a latin letter, no digit and no Russian letter: «IKEA», «Wi-Fi»); "has_latin"; "only_digits" (a number: «2», «1,5», «-5»); "has_digits"; "mixed" (a digit and a letter: «iphone15»).
pattern: for "starts", "ends" and "contains", a word part or a list of them, any one is enough; case and ё do not count.

Example: semkit read --text "диван ikea" extract-word-content only_latin write -
-> ikea

extract-word-content keeps only what the matcher finds in the working column; an empty cell where it finds nothing.

options.name: --kind
options.description: "starts", "ends", "contains" (with pattern); "only_latin" (a latin letter, no digit and no Russian letter: «IKEA», «Wi-Fi»); "has_latin"; "only_digits" (a number: «2», «1,5», «-5»); "has_digits"; "mixed" (a digit and a letter: «iphone15»).

options.name: --pattern
options.description: for "starts", "ends" and "contains", a word part or a list of them, any one is enough; case and ё do not count. Items: a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line, or the first column of a table) or @NAME of a list.

options.name: --as
options.description: Write the result to a new column NAME and keep the working column as it is.

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: "starts", "ends", "contains" (with pattern); "only_latin" (a latin letter, no digit and no Russian letter: «IKEA», «Wi-Fi»); "has_latin"; "only_digits" (a number: «2», «1,5», «-5»); "has_digits"; "mixed" (a digit and a letter: «iphone15»). The same as --kind KIND.
